div.div: Start here if you only want to see work assigned to you. Turn it on to hide other people's records from the chart, KPIs, bottom buttons, views, and reports (including linked Sales when a map is active). Leave it off to see the full team picture.
Use this section to build the chart. Everything below (Chart Model, Group By, Measures, and Data to Include) belongs here and changes the chart only — not KPIs, bottom buttons, views, or reports.
Pick which records feed the chart — for example Pipeline or Sales Orders. The left button label and screen change with this choice so they always match. Leave empty for the dashboard default.
Choose how the chart is split — for example by stage, salesperson, or team. Add more than one tag to go deeper (the first tag is the top level).
Choose what number the chart shows — for example how many records, or expected revenue. Leave empty to count records.
Still under Graph Configuration. Tick which record types go into the chart — for example Pipeline, Leads, or both.

Narrow data by date and custom rules. Date rows follow the selected Chart Model (each model can offer different dates). These filters apply to the chart, KPIs, bottom buttons, views, and reports (including linked Sales when available).
Still under Filters. Add your own rule when months and years are not enough — for example only high-probability deals.

field.name: help
field.p: Create a dashboard for any Odoo model.

Click New to open the create wizard, then edit in Studio. Use Import Template for a .dashboard.json file. Click a row or Customize to reopen Studio. Administrators can open the classic Advanced form when needed.
